about: Traits every species carries (genes 16-31, after its own loci; a species' locus with the same id is used instead). Each is quantitative: two values, the mean shows. `h` is its heritability: the share of its spread that comes from genes; the rest is the animal's own chance (development, food), not passed on. A species' gene file sets each one's mean and spread under `traits`, a breed or habitat its own under `quantitative`.

loci.name: Size
loci.about: small to big for its kind and sex

loci.name: White extent
loci.about: less to more white, where there is white (many genes besides the spotting ones)

loci.name: Mark size
loci.about: fine to bold marks: stripes, spots, bands

loci.name: Mark density
loci.about: sparse to crowded: how much of the coat the marks cover

loci.name: Mark edge
loci.about: smooth to ragged edges (giraffe spots: inherited)

loci.name: Mark stretch
loci.about: round to drawn out along the body

loci.name: Horns
loci.about: smaller to bigger horns, crests, frills

loci.name: Temperament
loci.about: calm to skittish: how near a walker comes before it runs (heritable in part, as boldness is in animals)
